paragraphs.text: A loose leaf [red tea](red:definition) from Yunnan, made in 2016. It is the fully oxidised tea that English calls black: once the leaf is broken, its own enzymes turn it from green to reddish brown. Red tea from this province is known as [Dian Hong](dian-hong:definition), made from Yunnan's large-leaf trees. The style dates from the war years: China was cut off from its eastern tea regions and needed a new red tea to sell abroad, so Feng Shaoqiu made a trial batch in Shunning, now Fengqing, in late 1938.

At ten years old, this lot sits well outside the usual window. The trade drinks Yunnan red within its first one to three years and [keeps it for freshness](dian-hong:ageing) rather than for age, so a decade is well past what the style is kept for.

brewing.text: Dian Hong takes hot water, roughly 90 to 100°C. A common start is about 5 grams to 100 ml, with short steeps that lengthen slowly as the leaf opens.

notice.text: A full, sweet cup, often described as malty, with chocolate or cocoa and honey notes and sometimes something floral. The liquor runs golden to bright red, and a good grade has little bitterness.
